name: Sum rule
summary: Splitting with a W-node, applying weights r and s to the branches and merging gives weight r+s.
description:
The W-node (black triangle) with one input and $n$ outputs maps $|0\rangle \mapsto |0\cdots 0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle \mapsto |10\cdots0\rangle + |010\cdots0\rangle + \cdots + |0\cdots01\rangle$: it spreads a single excitation over its outputs in all possible ways. The small dot marks its input leg.

Write $r$ for the two-legged white vertex (Z-box) $\mathrm{diag}(1, r)$. Splitting a wire with a W-node, applying $r$ and $s$ to the two branches and merging them with a W-node gives $\mathrm{diag}(1, r + s)$, because the excitation goes through exactly one of the branches. Together with [weighted spider fusion](../zw-weighted-fusion/), which multiplies labels, this is how the ring structure of $R$ is encoded in the $R$-labelled ZW-calculus: addition is convolution with respect to the W Hopf algebra.

The rule generalises to any number of branches, giving the sum of all labels. In the planar W-calculus of Carette, Moutot, Perez and Vilmart it reads: two parallel edges with weights $r$ and $s$ between two W-nodes can be replaced by one edge with weight $r+s$.
parameter_notes: Shown with two branches; holds for any number of branches.

source.location: Chapter 5, Section 5.2 (list of rules of the ZW calculus), rule $rng_+^{r,s}$
